title: Mitigating Surgical Data Imbalance with Dual-Prediction Video Diffusion Model
claim: Real-world data are heavily skewed toward some classes, hurting rare ones; adding our synthetic samples closes the gap and improves accuracy.
layout: 2 regions: left illustrated scene with bar plots, right dot-and-arrow gains plot
description: The left panel is a rounded light-blue box. It shows a cartoon surgeon performing laparoscopic surgery. A dashed line links the surgeon's gaze to a monitor showing the internal anatomy. A brace leads from the monitor to a fan of overlapping surgical video frames labeled 'Surgical video feed'. Below the frames are two bar charts, one purple for surgical gestures and one orange for surgical actions. Solid bars show real data and hatched grey segments show synthetic SurgiFlowVid samples. The hatched segments fill the rare classes up to the level of the common ones. A legend sits at the bottom. The right panel is a plot titled 'Surgical action recognition'. For each rare action it shows a baseline marker connected by a vertical line to a star marker for Real + SurgiFlowVid. Green arrows label the gains of 19%, 11% and 7%.
caption: Data challenge in the surgical domain. During a laparoscopic procedure, the surgeon operates via the endoscopic video feed (video on the monitor). ML models can leverage these videos for providing guidance through surgical scene understanding. However, the datasets are skewed as shown in the bar plots. We aim to mitigate data imbalance with synthetic samples. The right plot shows improvements from adding samples generated from our approach (SurgiFlowVid).
abstract: Surgical video datasets are essential for scene understanding, enabling procedural modeling and intra-operative support. However, these datasets are often heavily imbalanced, with rare actions and tools under-represented, which limits the robustness of downstream models. We address this challenge with $SurgiFlowVid$, a sparse and controllable video diffusion framework for generating surgical videos of under-represented classes. Our approach introduces a dual-prediction diffusion module that jointly denoises RGB frames and optical flow, providing temporal inductive biases to improve motion modeling from limited samples. In addition, a sparse visual encoder conditions the generation process on lightweight signals (e.g., sparse segmentation masks or RGB frames), enabling controllability without dense annotations. We validate our approach on three surgical datasets across tasks including action recognition, tool presence detection, and laparoscope motion prediction. Synthetic data generated by our method yields consistent gains of 10-20% over competitive baselines, establishing $SurgiFlowVid$ as a promising strategy to mitigate data imbalance and advance surgical video understanding methods.
